content: Nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in patients with anuria, oliguria, or significant renal impairment, specifically when creatinine clearance is less than 60 mL per minute or when serum creatinine levels are clinically significantly elevated. This is because impaired renal function increases the risk of drug toxicity due to reduced excretion of the medication. The drug is also contraindicated in pregnant patients at term (38–42 weeks of gestation), during labor and delivery, or when labor is imminent. This is due to the risk of hemolytic anemia in the neonate, which can occur as a result of immature erythrocyte enzyme systems, specifically glutathione instability. Similarly, nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in neonates under one month of age for the same reason—an increased risk of hemolytic anemia due to immature erythrocyte enzyme systems. MacroBID (a formulation of nitrofurantoin) is contraindicated in patients with a history of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction that was previously associated with nitrofurantoin use. Additionally, MacroBID is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to nitrofurantoin.
